summary.oneLiner: One of the largest specialised EPC companies with a global presence across power transmission & distribution, buildings & factories, water supply & treatment, railways, oil & gas infrastructure, urban mobility, highways and airports.
summary.business: KPIL is a diversified global EPC (engineering, procurement, construction) company operating across six business verticals -- Power Transmission & Distribution, Buildings & Factories, Water, Railways, Oil & Gas, and Infrastructure (highways/airports/metros). It serves government and private power utility companies, top-tier real estate developers, state/central governments and municipal bodies, and industrial clients, with operations spanning more than 75 countries and exports contributing about 30% of turnover.

Buildings & Factories: Residential, commercial and institutional buildings (incl. hospitals, educational facilities)
Composite structural construction and area development
Water: Water supply, storage and distribution pipelines
Railways: Dedicated rail corridors and rapid rail systems (emerging)
Infrastructure: Metro rail corridor stations and transit terminals/hubs

currentContext.strengths: Integrated EPC platform spanning in-house design, engineering, fabrication, construction and commissioning across six diversified business verticals|Engineering/technology leadership: first Indian EPC company to erect a 765 KV Double Circuit Transmission Tower (~47 MT) in a single day; first EPC company globally outside China to implement the Double Arm Gin Pole (DAGP) tower-erection system|Asset base built via ~INR 3,000 crore invested over the past five years in construction capabilities, manufacturing capacity, mechanisation and digital integration, supporting execution certainty on large, complex, high-entry-barrier projects|Trust-led customer relationships with a growing share of repeat orders from marquee customers|45-year operating legacy; workforce of 28,600+ across 50+ nationalities; presence across 75+ countries
currentContext.strategies: Expanding capabilities across next-generation infrastructure segments -- HVDC transmission systems, underground tunnelling, design-build Buildings & Factories, high-rise developments, data centres and industrial infrastructure -- to strengthen positioning as a comprehensive EPC solutions provider.|Railways/Urban Infrastructure strategy is to actively expand into high-speed rail, dedicated freight corridors and rapid transit systems, while maintaining a selective approach towards conventional railway projects.|Buildings & Factories growth strategy centred on large-format, design-build projects across residential, institutional, commercial buildings and data centres; design-build projects now account for nearly 50% of the B&F portfolio.|Oil & Gas strategy is to increase international market exposure, building on the ongoing execution of a major Saudi Arabia project to reinforce its Middle East presence.|Urban Infrastructure strategy centred on metro rail systems, airports and next-generation transit infrastructure, backed by investment in owned Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs).|Diversified portfolio strategy across six core/emerging business verticals aligned to global infrastructure megatrends, supported by backward-integrated manufacturing (in-house transmission tower manufacturing) and end-to-end execution capabilities.|Asia Pacific strategy focused on scaling urban mobility (five metro systems), airports, water infrastructure and digital infrastructure (data centres) alongside core T&D and buildings work.|Dividend payments are governed by a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI LODR Regulation 43A), unchanged during the year; the Board recommended a final dividend of INR 11 per equity share (550% of face value) for FY26, subject to AGM approval. Alongside this, the Company pursued selective portfolio rationalisation during the year -- consolidating control of a Middle East subsidiary by acquiring the JV partner's remaining 35% stake in Kalpataru Projects Arabia Company (making it wholly owned), while divesting a non-core road asset (100% stake in Vindhyachal Expressway Pvt. Limited sold to Actis Atlantic Holdings Limited).
currentContext.expansion: Capex/expansion content in this bundle is concentrated in energy-efficiency and renewable self-generation investment rather than core EPC/manufacturing capacity addition. KPIL operates manufacturing plants at Gandhinagar and Raipur and two biomass power plants -- Padampur Power Plant (PPP) and Uniara Power Plant (UPP). During FY 2025-26 the Company commissioned a 3 MWp solar photovoltaic power plant at Uniara Power Plant, which exported approximately 5,049 MWh to the grid during the year. Across plants and project sites the Company expanded solar photovoltaic and solar-powered lighting deployment, raising total owned installed solar capacity to over 6.18 MWp (comprising 5.68 MWp across the four plants and 0.50 MWp across project sites), alongside VFD-enabled compressors, battery-operated material handling equipment, LED lighting and other efficiency upgrades across the T&D, Oil & Gas, Buildings & Factories, Railways, Urban Infrastructure and Water businesses. Separately, the Company is preparing for the Environment (Construction and Demolition) Waste Management Rules, 2025 (effective 1 April 2026), which are expected to bring Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements into scope; during FY26 the Company was in a planning/readiness stage, developing an EPR compliance roadmap and exploring engagement with authorised recyclers and waste-management agencies.

risks.note: EPC operations are exposed to execution delays, supply chain disruptions and site-level challenges, potentially leading to cost overruns and revenue impact.
Exposure to interest rate fluctuations, foreign exchange volatility and liquidity constraints; project delays and unfavourable payment terms may increase working capital requirements.

risks.risk: Commodity price and currency fluctuation risk
risks.note: Volatility in prices of key inputs such as steel, cement, copper and aluminium can impact project costs and profitability, especially under fixed-price contracts; currency moves further affect financial performance.
Risk of payment delays or counterparty failure to meet contractual obligations, especially in long-cycle projects or volatile geographies.

Company has footprints in over 75 countries with active projects in over 30 countries; unstable geopolitical situations affect project execution cycles and costs, and political instability in a country/region exposes the Company to delayed collections or non-payment default.

Operating across diverse infrastructure sectors and geographies, including remote or high-risk terrains and varying regulatory environments, exposes the Company to EHS risk; lapses may lead to legal liabilities, operational disruptions, reputational damage and increased costs.
Increased digitisation exposes the Company to cybersecurity threats that may impact business continuity and data integrity.

risks.risk: Subsidiary going-concern flag (Shree Shubham Logistics Limited)
risks.note: Statutory auditors' consolidated CARO report drew attention to accumulated losses at Shree Shubham Logistics Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary), noting the Company represents it can meet liabilities as they fall due based on committed cash flows from sale of non-core assets and continuing credit facility availability; auditors state this is not an assurance of future viability.

one-line thesis: KPIL is capitalizing on India's aggressive infrastructure push with strong order inflows in power transmission and water projects, driving margin expansion and cash flow improvement. The company's disciplined execution and low debt position make it a high-conviction play in mid-cap EPC space.

guidance: Revenue growth of 15-18% FY27; EBITDA margin target of 12-13%; orderbook to cross ₹30,000 Cr by FY27 end
order book & pipeline: ₹28,500 Cr as of Mar 2026 (up from ₹22,100 Cr in FY25); new orders of ₹6,400 Cr in Q4FY26; 65% from power transmission, 20% from water, 15% from industrial

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global power infrastructure investment is entering a multi-decade expansion cycle across generation, storage and T&D, with annual global investment in power infrastructure projected to expand from USD 631 billion (2024) to USD 1.1 trillion by 2050 (PwC).
- India's National Electricity Plan targets peak demand of 458 GW by 2032 and estimates INR 9.2 trillion of T&D infrastructure investment, expanding the transmission network from 5.06 lakh ckm (Mar-2025) to 6.48 lakh ckm (2032).
- India's renewable energy target of 500 GW capacity by 2030 is driving grid expansion and transmission investment needs.
- Middle East / GCC T&D capex is accelerating (Saudi Arabia targeting ~0.16 million ckm of transmission and ~1.1 million ckm of distribution network additions by 2030), supporting KPIL's international T&D order pipeline.
- India oil & gas: PNGRB Vision 2040 outlines two national gas grid transmission projects plus 19 pipeline corridor projects (~8,000 km, ~USD 39.73 billion investment) and the March-2026 Products Distribution Order aims to expand PNG networks -- both seen as opportunity for pipeline/LNG EPC.
- India's National Infrastructure Pipeline has scaled to ~14,563 projects (from ~6,800 at inception) worth ~INR 213 trillion (from INR 111 trillion), supporting sustained EPC demand in civil construction.
- Rapid urbanisation (India's urban population share expected to rise from 36% to 40% by 2030) is driving sustained residential, commercial and industrial real estate demand feeding the Buildings & Factories order pipeline.
- Buildings & Factories revenue grew ~19% YoY in FY26, driven by real estate, industrial capex and digital-infrastructure (data centre) demand, with design-build projects now ~50% of the portfolio.
- Railways segment is deliberately shifting mix away from conventional railway projects towards metro rail and high-speed rail opportunities.
- Africa T&D market described as on a steady upward trajectory on rising electricity demand, renewables integration and regional interconnectivity push -- a market where KPIL is already active across 10+ countries.
- Europe's power demand is forecast to grow 1.5-2% annually from 2026 (after 15 years of decline) on electrification, EVs and data centres, with capex on T&D infrastructure expected at EUR1.2-1.4 trillion over 2026-35 -- a market KPIL is expanding execution in (e.g., Sweden, Brazil, other geographies).
- Consolidated order book of INR 65,457 crore as of 31 March 2026 -- described as highest ever -- including subsidiaries in EPC business and excluding fairly placed bids; orders received of INR 26,400 crore during FY26.
- Power Transmission & Distribution is the largest segment, accounting for approximately 44% of KPIL's total order book as of 31 March 2026; segment order book trend was INR 20,678 cr (FY24) -> INR 26,671 cr (FY25) -> INR 28,572 cr (FY26).
- Buildings & Factories order book trend: INR 11,021 cr (FY24) -> INR 14,095 cr (FY25) -> INR 18,295 cr (FY26).
- Water Supply & Irrigation order book trend: INR 10,667 cr (FY24) -> INR 9,573 cr (FY25) -> INR 7,486 cr (FY26), a declining trend.
- Oil & Gas order book trend: INR 9,031 cr (FY24) -> INR 7,699 cr (FY25) -> INR 4,578 cr (FY26), a declining trend.
- Urban Infrastructure order book trend: INR 3,033 cr (FY24) -> INR 3,074 cr (FY25) -> INR 4,143 cr (FY26).
- Railways order book trend: INR 3,985 cr (FY24) -> INR 3,383 cr (FY25) -> INR 2,382 cr (FY26), a declining trend.
- Asia Pacific order book exceeds INR 40,000 crore (USD 4.7+ billion), with over 200 EPC projects under execution across the region, including five underground/elevated metro systems.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin improved to 11.8% (FY25: 10.2%) due to better project mix, reduced subcontractor dependency, and cost optimization in transmission line execution

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Net cash position of ₹120 Cr; priority is debt reduction (zero net debt target by FY27), followed by strategic M&A in water EPC; no dividend declared

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Capex/expansion content in this bundle is concentrated in energy-efficiency and renewable self-generation investment rather than core EPC/manufacturing capacity addition. KPIL operates manufacturing plants at Gandhinagar and Raipur and two biomass power plants -- Padampur Power Plant (PPP) and Uniara Power Plant (UPP). During FY 2025-26 the Company commissioned a 3 MWp solar photovoltaic power plant at Uniara Power Plant, which exported approximately 5,049 MWh to the grid during the year. Across plants and project sites the Company expanded solar photovoltaic and solar-powered lighting deployment, raising total owned installed solar capacity to over 6.18 MWp (comprising 5.68 MWp across the four plants and 0.50 MWp across project sites), alongside VFD-enabled compressors, battery-operated material handling equipment, LED lighting and other efficiency upgrades across the T&D, Oil & Gas, Buildings & Factories, Railways, Urban Infrastructure and Water businesses. Separately, the Company is preparing for the Environment (Construction and Demolition) Waste Management Rules, 2025 (effective 1 April 2026), which are expected to bring Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements into scope; during FY26 the Company was in a planning/readiness stage, developing an EPR compliance roadmap and exploring engagement with authorised recyclers and waste-management agencies.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and optimistic; emphasized execution discipline, strong client relationships with Power Grid Corp and state utilities, and visibility into 18-24 months of work

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated EPC platform spanning in-house design, engineering, fabrication, construction and commissioning across six diversified business verticals
- Engineering/technology leadership: first Indian EPC company to erect a 765 KV Double Circuit Transmission Tower (~47 MT) in a single day; first EPC company globally outside China to implement the Double Arm Gin Pole (DAGP) tower-erection system
- Asset base built via ~INR 3,000 crore invested over the past five years in construction capabilities, manufacturing capacity, mechanisation and digital integration, supporting execution certainty on large, complex, high-entry-barrier projects
- Trust-led customer relationships with a growing share of repeat orders from marquee customers
- 45-year operating legacy; workforce of 28,600+ across 50+ nationalities; presence across 75+ countries

risks.body: Delay in government clearances for transmission projects; currency volatility on overseas contracts (12% of revenue); labor shortages in key states

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: KPIL has quietly built a proprietary prefabrication tech for transmission towers, reducing on-site labor needs by 30% — a hidden cost advantage competitors haven't replicated

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Portfolio exit] Debt tables carry the note "Gross Debt exclude interest-free loan received pursuant to agreements in relation to the divestment of T&D Assets", and the net-debt series is stated as "excluding interest-free loan pursuant to divestment of T&D assets" — the deck discloses no size, counterparty or date for this divestment.
- [Non-core wind-down] Revenue from Road SPVs and the Brazil subsidiary is excluded from headline growth because they have "no/minimal operations in FY27"; that revenue fell from ₹283 crore (Q1 FY26) to ₹12 crore (Q1 FY27), with Brazil Business / Fasttel specifically going from ₹217 crore to ₹1 crore. "Others" is described as mainly Road SPVs, Shree Shubham Logistics (SSL) and a Biomass Plant.
- [Segment softness] Water execution "remained slow given lower collections in JJM projects" (revenue -7% YoY) and Railways revenue was -23% YoY, described as "in-line with order book and focus on project closures"; T&D growth came "despite supply chain constraints in international markets".
- [Shareholding] As on 30 June 2026: Promoters 33.6%, DIIs 44.8%, FIIs/FPI 10.8%, Public & Others 10.8%.
- [Leadership] Manish Mohnot is MD & CEO, S K Tripathi Deputy MD, Sanjay Dalmia Executive Director, Amit Uplenchwar Director - Strategy Business Group, Ram Patodia CFO and M.A. Baraiya CHRO; Mofatraj P. Munot is Founder & Non-Executive Chairman with Parag M. Munot as Director.
